purpose: Test whether a named-world rule stored only in notebook context affects later video output without repeating it in the immediate shot prompt.

setup.conditions: Two fresh matched test contexts, isolated from production chats/history and existing dog references.
setup.commonWorldSource: Bellglass is a small fantasy settlement with outdoor village courtyards. A local resident can cross the courtyard in daylight.
setup.onlyTreatmentAddition: Every outdoor Bellglass scene includes an ordinary dog in the background wearing a vivid blue collar. Barking is part of its ambient location audio.
setup.control: Same common world source without the dog paragraph; do not add an explicit no-dog rule.
setup.media: Prefer text-to-video to avoid dog imagery or an exact-first-frame preservation requirement confounding object addition. If a reference is necessary, use the same animal-free reference and a compatible role in both conditions.

sharedImmediatePrompt: On the home world of Bellglass, show one continuous wide shot of a local resident crossing a village courtyard in daylight. Use a gentle forward camera move and natural location ambience. No music or narration.
beforeExecution: Verify actual supported generation surface/model, duration/aspect ratio/output count, native audio support, quota/cost and allowed total spend. Unknowns remain unknown until observed.
Use identical supported settings; record the source text and exact prompt separately. Do not restate the dog rule in either immediate prompt or carry a dog-test discussion into either context.
Record any exposed assembled generator inputs; distinguish notebook retrieval from injected prompt text and reference conditioning.

scoring.visual: Independent playback: dog actually visible in background; blue collar separately recorded as distinctive canary detail.
scoring.audio: Listen to actual exported audio for barking, separate from a model report or Mute control.
scoring.outcomes: Capture pass/partial/absent/unknown for each criterion in each condition; record frame/timestamp evidence.
scoring.interpretation: A treatment-specific distinctive dog plus barking supports context influence; it is not proof of universal compliance. A single absence is inconclusive: retrieval, prompt assembly, instruction conflict, renderer omission, audio support or randomness can cause it. Dog appearing in control reduces specificity.
scoring.repetition: Any additional comparison or direct-prompt positive control needs a later bounded decision; no automatic retries/batches.
